identity.title: The atomic gas of star-forming galaxies at z ∼ 0.05 as revealed by the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Radio Telescope

paper_type_evidence.quote: Together with previous Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) CO($J=1-0$) observations, the Hi data provides crucial information to measure the gas mass and dynamics.

question.value: What is the atomic gas (HI) content and dynamics of four z~0.05 VALES star-forming galaxies observed with FAST, compared with their ALMA CO(1-0) data?

evidence.quote: we aim to study the atomic gas content, via the Hi  21 cm emission line, in low-$z$ star formation galaxies taken from the Valparaíso ALMA/APEX Line Emission Survey (VALES).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00530.S.
The CO($J=1-0$) and CO($J=2-1$) emission lines have been observed using the Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimiter Array (cite: Villanueva2017)

provided.value: New HI 21 cm spectra with the 19-beam L-band receiver (central beam), ON-OFF tracking

evidence.quote: We were allocated 10 hours in L-band with the 19-Beam receiver during the FAST Commissioning Phase

provided.value: Archival HI spectrum for one target for comparison

evidence.quote: we include one source with ALFALFA measurements (HATLASJ083601.5+002617) to check consistency and the relative performance of the FAST telescope.
(cite: Cheng2018), respectively.

what.value: CO(1-0) luminosities, line widths and dynamical masses from ALMA/VALES

evidence.quote: In (cite: Molina2019), we presented a dynamical analysis to 39 VALES galaxies using the spatial extension of the CO($J=1-0$) emission.

what.value: Stellar mass, radius and photometry from GAMA structure catalogue and H-ATLAS catalogue

evidence.quote: We adopt the stellar mass, radius and the photometry from GAMA galaxy structure catalogue (cite: Kelvin2012) and $H$-ATLAS catalogue (cite: 2016MNRAS.462.3146V).

what.value: ALFALFA HI flux and FWHM for HATLASJ083601.5+002617

evidence.loc: 4.1 Comparison with a previous ALFALFA result
evidence.quote: The integrated flux of the Arecibo spectrum given in (cite: Haynes2018) is $1.68 \pm 0.14$ mJy km s$^{-1}$

what.value: FAST noise-diode flux calibration and 14.86 K/Jy conversion

evidence.quote: We adopt a 14.86 K Jy$^{-1}$ conversion factor, which has an accuracy of the order of 10% (cite: Jiang2020).

what.value: HI radius from HI mass relation

evidence.quote: the $R_{\rm H\textsc{i}}$ can be estimated from $M _{\rm H\textsc{i}}$ using the relation derived by (cite: 2016MNRAS.460.2143W).

what.value: HI inclination assumed equal to Ks-band inclination

evidence.quote: if we assume the Ks band image and Hi have a similar inclination angle (cite: Molina2019)

unstated_but_needed: ALMA CO(1-0) calibration and imaging details (all from earlier papers)
Inclination values and HI radii used per galaxy
H2 mass conversion (alpha_CO) for baryon mass
Baseline fit and RFI flagging details

analysis_steps.goal: Reduce and calibrate FAST ON-OFF spectra

method.value: Noise-diode calibration, inverse-variance weighted mean of ON and OFF spectra, ON-OFF, sinusoid+linear baseline fit, LSR correction, polarisations combined

evidence.quote: We subtract the baseline using model-fit based on a sinusoidal plus a linear function

key_parameters.value: 14.86 K/Jy conversion; 10 min chunks; baseline fitted 1372-1376 MHz

evidence.quote: The data is reduced in chunks of 10 min.

validation.value: Compared with ALFALFA spectrum and checked two polarisations

evidence.quote: We do not find significant differences in polarisation

method.value: Resample to 20 km/s channels, sum channels within FWZI; M_HI = 2.35e5 D^2/(1+z) integral S dV; upper limit 5 x rms x 300 W300

evidence.quote: derive the integrated Hi flux by summing over the velocity channels within Full Width at Zero Intensity (FWZI)
the $10\% \times \rm flux$ would account for the uncertainty of the flux calibration

validation.value: Consistency with ALFALFA and with empirical HI mass relations

evidence.loc: 4.1 Comparison with a previous ALFALFA result
evidence.quote: This indicates a reasonable flux calibration for the FAST 19-beam receiver in this commissioning phase experiment.

method.value: M_dyn = (FWHM/2/sin theta)^2 R_HI / G with R_HI from HI mass-size relation

evidence.quote: $M_{\rm dyn}^{\rm H\textsc{i}} = ({\rm FWHM/2/\sin \theta})^2 R_{\rm H\textsc{i}} / G$
We do not have inclination information of the Hi gas.

results_numeric.quantity: rms at 1.7 km/s for 5 min ON (GAMA 214184)

findings_qualitative.value: HI and CO(1-0) line profiles are similar in width.

evidence.quote: We find that the CO($J=1-0$) and Hi emission line profiles are similar.

claims.hypothesis: FAST commissioning data give HI fluxes consistent with ALFALFA
claims.experiment: Compared FAST and ALFALFA spectrum of HATLASJ083601.5+002617
claims.finding: FAST flux calibration is reasonable and sensitivity is comparable to ALFALFA with 5 min

evidence.loc: 4.1 Comparison with a previous ALFALFA result
evidence.quote: both values consistent with our results

claims.hypothesis: HI traces more dark-matter-dominated mass than CO
claims.experiment: Compared HI dynamical mass with baryon and CO dynamical mass
claims.result: M_dyn^HI about an order of magnitude above baryon mass
claims.finding: HI traces the dark matter halo

evidence.quote: is an order of magnitude higher than the baryon mass

limitations_admitted.value: rms does not decrease as 1/sqrt(t), possibly pointing jitter or weak interference in commissioning

evidence.quote: The rms declines with the on-target integration time, but not in the manner of $\propto 1/\sqrt{t}$

referee_caveats_inferred: HI dynamical mass relies on assumed inclination and statistical HI radius
Only four galaxies; unresolved single-dish HI
ALMA data used only via earlier papers
